bachelor planning

General Studies bachelor’s with an aligned concentration

A broad completion family to compare when prior learning spans several subjects. Assemble concentration, liberal-arts, laboratory and required Charter Oak work into one current audit.

What makes this route worth exploring

  • Flexible concentration/elective allocation
  • Prior-learning evaluation
  • Cornerstone/capstone sequencing

What needs to be confirmed

  • The historical guide does not establish current alternative-credit acceptance.
  • A lecture/lab pair must meet the actual matching rule.
  • Concentration and upper-level constraints can bind before the transfer ceiling.

Eligibility and your situation

  • Confirm active concentration and current credit-source acceptance.
  • Ask how older work counts toward level and subject requirements.

A practical sequence

  1. Select degree, concentration and catalog.
  2. Obtain official prior-credit evaluation.
  3. Assemble GE, liberal-arts, concentration, upper-level and residency blocks.
  4. Map proposed outside work with current approval.
  5. Schedule required Charter Oak courses and remaining gaps.
  6. Complete final audit and graduation.

Your next useful actions

  • Send the same inventory used for other candidates.
  • Request current concentration and institutional-course rules.
  • Replace historical equivalencies with current receiving-school evidence.

Official & supporting sources

  • Charter Oak transfer admissions
  • Researched Charter Oak degree-plan frameworkChecked 2026-10-30
Ask for an individual evaluation.

Credit limits, degree placement, institutional-credit requirements, and professional eligibility are separate decisions. Use the current catalog and get the receiving school’s written confirmation.
